newsitem.title: USA: Wire-transfer rules set to cut down on drugs - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Wire-transfer rules set to cut down on drugs - NYT.

text.p: The Clinton administration is expected to set up a reporting system of large wire transfers by street-corner, check-cashing services to places outside the United States as a way to cut back on drug trafficking, the New York Times said on Monday.

The Times said the new rules were expected to be announced on Monday and were aimed at making it more difficult for drug cartels to move their profits from the United States to Colombia and other drug centres in Latin America.

Under the new rules, cash-checking services would be required to report wire transfers of more than $750 outside the United States to the Treasury. Currently, transfers of $10,000 or more are required to fill out government paperwork that includes information about the sender.

Banks, which operate under separate rules that require reports of suspicious activity, would be exempt. However, they would still be required to file reports of international transactions of more than $10,000, the Times said.
The Times said that non-banks are concerned the new requirements would create too much paperwork.
